svg.title: SQL logical order of execution
svg.desc: One query traced step by step, with the rows that exist after each step. 1: FROM flights and INNER JOIN airlines bring in 8 flights and 3 airlines; ON pairs each flight with its airline's name. 2: WHERE dep_delay > 0 drops f3 and f7, leaving 6 rows. 3: GROUP BY name forms 3 groups: American with 1 flight, Delta with 2, United with 3. 4 and 5: COUNT(*) is computed per group and HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 drops American. 6: SELECT outputs name and n_flights for Delta (2) and United (3). 7: ORDER BY n_flights DESC puts United first. 8: LIMIT 1 keeps only United, 3.
svg.text: Logical order: the clauses run in a different order than you write them
Each box shows the table that exists after that step. Read left to right, one row of boxes at a time.
name comes from airlines: each flight
is matched to its carrier's row
each group collapses to one row
4: COUNT(*) is computed for each group
Red numbers are the step in which each clause runs. SELECT is written first but runs sixth, so a column
alias such as n_flights works in ORDER BY but not in WHERE, GROUP BY, or HAVING. That is why HAVING repeats COUNT(*).
